title: A Night Walk by the Lake
paragraphs: On the last night of the school camp, Mr. Lin led the class on a short walk. First they paddled across a quiet lake in the dark. A splash made everyone jump, but it was only a [[beaver|L7-1947]] hurrying away. Then they pulled the boats [[ashore|L7-2047]] and tied them to a tree. The paths were muddy because rain [[runoff|L7-2041]] had washed over them all afternoon, so the students wore their boots. Ben, who was afraid of the dark, stayed close to the hand [[crank|L7-1948]] lamp.

Under the thick [[canopy|L7-2048]] of leaves, no moonlight could reach the ground. Every sound seemed bigger than it was. The wind outside was nearly a [[gale|L7-1938]], and branches cracked above them. Mr. Lin acted as the [[lookout|L7-1951]] at the front of the line. Somewhere ahead, something seemed to [[lurk|L7-2035]] between the trees. "It is only a [[spooky|L7-2042]] story," Mr. Lin said, but Ben felt a wave of [[adrenaline|L7-2046]] rush through his body, and his hands went [[numb|L7-2037]] from the cold and the fear.

Then a pair of round yellow eyes appeared. A soft shape glided over their heads with perfect [[stealth|L7-2043]], making no sound at all, and landed on a branch. It was an owl. The whole class let out a breath together. "This [[locality|L7-2034]] is famous for owls," Mr. Lin explained. "I was hoping we would see one." Ben began to [[chuckle|L7-0184]], and soon everybody was laughing so hard that the owl flew away, offended.

On Monday, during [[recess|L7-2040]], Ben told the story to his friends. Each time he told it, the owl grew a [[tad|L7-2044]] larger and the forest a little darker. By the end of the week, the owl was the size of a dog, and Ben was a hero. Mr. Lin only smiled when he heard. A good camp, he thought, is one where fear turns into a good story.
zh: 在學校露營的最後一個晚上，林老師帶全班進行一小段散步。他們先在黑暗中划船越過一座安靜的湖。一陣水花聲嚇了大家一跳，但那只是一隻匆匆游走的海狸。接著他們把船拉上岸，綁在一棵樹上。因為整個下午雨水徑流沖過小徑，路面很泥濘，所以學生們都穿了靴子。怕黑的阿本緊緊靠近那盞手搖燈。
在濃密的樹冠底下，月光照不到地面。每個聲音都顯得比實際更大。外面的風幾乎像強風，樹枝在他們頭頂上喀喀作響。林老師擔任隊伍前頭的瞭望員。前方某處，似乎有什麼東西潛伏在樹木之間。「那只是個恐怖故事，」林老師說，但阿本感到一股腎上腺素衝過全身，他的雙手因為寒冷和恐懼而發麻。
接著出現了一雙圓圓的黃色眼睛。一個柔軟的身影無聲無息地滑過他們頭頂，悄悄地沒發出任何聲音，停在一根樹枝上。那是一隻貓頭鷹。全班同時鬆了一口氣。「這一帶以貓頭鷹聞名，」林老師解釋，「我本來就希望我們能看到一隻。」阿本開始輕聲笑，不久大家笑得太大聲，貓頭鷹被冒犯似地飛走了。
星期一下課時間，阿本把這個故事講給朋友聽。每講一次，貓頭鷹就變大一點，森林也變暗一點。到了週末，那隻貓頭鷹已經有一隻狗那麼大，而阿本成了英雄。林老師聽說後只是微笑。他心想，一次好的露營，就是讓恐懼變成一個好故事的露營。

title: A Day with a Pediatric Nurse
paragraphs: Ms. Huang has worked as a [[pediatric|L7-2039]] nurse for eleven years. Her hospital is a large [[tertiary|L7-1059]] center, which means it treats the most serious cases sent from smaller clinics in the area. "A child cannot explain what is wrong in medical words," she says. "You have to listen to the way they say it."

Her morning begins with a nine-year-old boy who fell during [[recess|L7-2040]] and hit his head on the ground. He has a mild [[concussion|L7-1999]], so he must rest in a quiet room and be watched closely. Every hour, Ms. Huang checks his eyes with a small light and asks him easy questions. When she asks about his favorite game, he answers, "Soccer, but I will not play it again." She cannot help but [[chuckle|L7-0184]]. "Give it a week," she tells him.

At noon, a girl arrives with sharp [[abdominal|L7-1969]] pain and [[nausea|L7-2021]]. Her face is pale, and her mother waits in the corridor with hands [[numb|L7-2037]] from worry. In moments like this, Ms. Huang feels a rush of [[adrenaline|L7-2046]], but she has learned to keep her voice calm and her movements slow. Frightened children watch the adults' faces, she explains, and they borrow whatever feeling they find there. Tests show an infection, and by evening, the girl is smiling again.

Not every patient is an emergency. Some children come every few months because of a [[thyroid|L7-2045]] that does not make enough of the chemicals that help the body grow. Others come for vaccines, which teach the body to make [[antibodies|L7-1996]] against dangerous diseases. Good [[ventilation|L7-1965]] in every room is also a rule, because fresh air helps stop germs from spreading. Down the hall, a boy who fell from his bike is proudly showing his friends the bright blue [[plaster|L7-0749]] on his broken arm, and they are lining up to sign it.

At the end of her shift, Ms. Huang writes her notes and washes her hands for the last time. She admits that the work is tiring. But then she thinks of the signatures on the blue plaster and the boy who will play soccer again. "Children heal faster than adults," she says. "I think it is because they believe that they will."
zh: 黃小姐擔任兒科護理師已經十一年。她任職的醫院是一家大型三級醫療中心，意思是它收治由地區內較小診所轉送來的最嚴重病例。「孩子沒辦法用醫學用語說明哪裡不對，」她說，「你得聽他們說話的方式。」
她的早晨從一位九歲男孩開始，他在下課休息時跌倒，頭撞到地面。他有輕微腦震盪，所以必須在安靜的房間休息並被密切觀察。每個小時，黃小姐都會用小燈檢查他的眼睛，並問他簡單的問題。當她問他最喜歡的遊戲時，他回答：「足球，但我不會再踢了。」她忍不住輕笑。「過一個星期再說吧，」她告訴他。
中午，一個女孩因劇烈腹痛和噁心來到醫院。她臉色蒼白，她的母親在走廊等著，雙手因擔心而發麻。在這樣的時刻，黃小姐會感到腎上腺素飆升，但她已學會保持聲音冷靜、動作緩慢。她解釋，受驚的孩子會觀察大人的臉，並借用他們在那裡找到的任何情緒。檢查顯示是感染，到了傍晚，這個女孩又露出了笑容。
並非每位病人都是急診。有些孩子每隔幾個月就來一次，因為甲狀腺分泌的幫助身體成長的化學物質不足。另一些孩子來打疫苗，疫苗能教身體製造對抗危險疾病的抗體。每個房間保持良好通風也是一條規定，因為新鮮空氣有助於阻止細菌傳播。走廊另一頭，一個從腳踏車上摔下來的男孩正得意地向朋友展示他手臂上亮藍色的石膏，他們排隊要簽名。
輪班結束時，黃小姐寫完紀錄，最後一次洗手。她承認這份工作很累。但她接著想起藍色石膏上的簽名，和那個將再次踢足球的男孩。「孩子比大人復原得快，」她說，「我想是因為他們相信自己會好。」
